items.notes: Context-map ownership and mapping maintainers are discussed; no explicit risk from unowned mappings.
Durable replay cursor and recovery after a lost ack; framed for stream items, not submitted job status.
Resequencer ordering and gap disposition; no split-message completion or partial-release rule.
Aggregator completeness condition and partial-failure policy are relevant; unknown part count is not addressed.
Compares cache placements; does not discuss expiration or the freshness promise.
Distinguishes expiration/eviction from refresh and explains that expiry alone does not refresh.
Explains async refresh returning a stored value while loading; directly bears on expiration vs freshness.
Cache invalidation and stale-after-write are relevant to stale edge copies; no purge or origin-removal specifics.
Optional-dependency isolation under load; not a parallel-run candidate failure and its user-response rule.
Dual-write atomicity between database and broker; does not address mirrored traffic or live shadow writes.
Runtime/lifecycle constraint row names dependency-version risk; no colocated sidecar lifecycle treatment.
Accepted-versus-completed outcomes support when polling is unneeded; polling is not discussed.
Readiness/liveness separation and the limit that a green probe does not prove readiness or routing answer the why.
Describes EDS endpoint fetching; no active health-check rationale.
Explains the relay lease/publish/complete loop relevant to a stuck relay; poison-row handling is not addressed.
Chapter-level framing of four patterns; no relay failure or poison-row operational guidance.
Cacheability/authorization contract and private-data misclassification explain the static-hosting mismatch.
Defines parallel run and its side-effect limits; the requested lower-overhead alternative is absent.
Shopify 2019 componentization context, but Wedge and how it surfaced dependencies are not in the excerpt.
JVM pauses appear as a wall-clock component; no Netflix GC account or load-amplification mechanism.
ByteBuf and descriptor leaks support off-heap memory pressure; heap-stable versus memory-limit link is implicit.
CPU utilization is called deceptive while requests wait; flame-graph insufficiency is not directly explained.
Gateway architecture choice and blocked-wait metrics; no CPU profiling or flame-graph limitation.
Retention/expiration after which resume cannot succeed directly answers what an offset reset cannot recover.
Index families and planner choice; no range-versus-hash partitioning comparison.
Query and distribution modelling; partitioning strategy is not discussed.
Quorum arithmetic shows added voters raise the vote threshold; write-capacity effect is not addressed.
Single-writer and per-aggregate alternatives are relevant; no explanation of shard write-capacity limits.
Authorization filtering and recall proof; incomplete relevance judgments are not addressed.
Defines Recall@k against independently judged relevant items, which is what the question asks.
Admission-control and queue bounds are relevant overload controls; priority-queue starvation is absent.
Shows overload dominated by timeouts at 0.05% rejection; the rejecting-most case is not explained.
Explains that reject rate is a poor overload signal and completed useful work is the measure.
Separating build/artifact/promotion boundaries and noting pipeline success does not prove deployment answers why.
Evidence for another digest or unapproved identity must not authorize promotion; directly on digest matching.
Same artifact-identity rationale: a successful run does not prove the intended artifact was deployed.
Progressive delivery versus schema compatibility is relevant to rollback coordination; GitOps reconciliation is absent.
Hermetic-test/non-hermetic-runtime and missing business mappings show what an inventory-free baseline loses.
State-ownership review is relevant; it does not say when an in-place runtime upgrade suffices.
Transition-state diagram keeps old authority until extraction; the reason for preserving it is not stated.
A reversal trigger exists when semantics cannot be preserved; source-side conditions are not discussed.
Negative cases cover scale and consumer SLA; no essential source-side condition.
Arrival rate versus capacity and the (120-80)x20 backlog arithmetic directly govern growth and drainage.
Defines arrival rate, service capacity, utilization, queue length and time in system.
Coexistence states and reconciliation backlog are relevant; no growth/drainage quantities.
Migration sequence and reversal triggers; no rollback traffic destination.
Model-family abstraction; no statement of where new traffic goes after rollback.
Netflix gateway connection scalability, not the cloud migration retrospective's motivating failure.
